Reading preferences for primary maths

Dyslexia-friendly maths practice with a clear reading mode.

Some children find crowded text or a busy screen harder to use. KickMaths includes a clearly labelled Dyslexia-friendly mode so families and teachers can try a more comfortable reading layout.

Play the free beta

What changes when you switch it on?

Font and spacing

The reading mode uses a familiar sans-serif font, clearer letter spacing and more space between lines. Text can be enlarged using browser zoom.

Softer reading surface

A softer background and clear text contrast reduce the brightness of large reading areas. The maths questions and rewards stay the same.

Less visual distraction

The reading layout reduces decorative movement. The game also provides a separate Reduce motion setting for a quieter screen.

How to enable it on the website and in the game.

  1. On this website, select Dyslexia-friendly mode in the header, or use the button above.
  2. In the game, open Settings or the grown-up area and select Dyslexia-friendly mode.
  3. Use Reduce motion separately if animations are distracting.
  4. Try the settings with the pupil and keep the combination they find easiest to use.

On the website, reading preferences are remembered only when you choose Remember preferences in the cookie banner. A setting can still be tried without saving it.

Reading support does not change the maths standard.

The same question, independent-answer rules and skill evidence apply in either layout. Choosing a more comfortable font does not cost credits, reduce XP or mark an answer as helped. Coach’s written explanations remain available when mathematical support is needed.

Designed to support choice.

Dyslexia affects people differently, and no single font works best for every pupil. These settings offer reading choices; they are not a diagnostic tool or a treatment. Parents, teachers and pupils can tell us which parts of the layout need improvement.

Frequently asked questions

Does KickMaths change the font for dyslexia-friendly mode?

Yes. The mode changes the reading font and spacing, uses a softer reading background and reduces decorative distraction. It is clearly labelled so users can find and compare it.

Is there audio or a read-aloud feature?

No. KickMaths uses visual questions and written explanations. Sound effects and spoken questions are not part of this version.

Can pupils with other reading needs use the mode?

Yes. Anyone can try the reading preferences and use the layout that is most comfortable.
